# Effect gems: balance model

Generated by `tools/gem-balance.py` from the owner's design in `specs/effect-gems.md`. Do not edit by hand: change the script and rerun it. Vanilla numbers come from the decompiled Minecraft 26.3 source and the script re-checks them against it.

## The formula in plain words

- Every effect is measured on one scale: **1.0 = the strongest vanilla potion level of that effect** (Speed II, Strength II, Regeneration II, Resistance IV from strong Turtle Master...). For on/off effects 1.0 is the full effect.
- **One gem's strength** = potion factor x base gem factor x enchant grade x armor material factor x matching-run factor. Each is at most 1.0.
- **Stacking:** a piece holds 3 gems, so 12 in all. The gems of one effect are lined up strongest first; the first counts fully, each next one 85% of the one before. The sum is scaled so that 12 perfect gems give exactly **0.95**. So a full kit of perfect gems is the only way to 0.95, and a stack can never beat 0.95 x its strongest gem: many weak gems stay weak.
- **The cap is 0.95**: 5% short of vanilla's best. Close enough that the endgame feels like a potion you never drink (Speed +38% instead of +40%), far enough that on/off effects still show it (5% of fire damage still lands; air lasts 5 minutes, not forever).
- **Potion form doesn't multiply**: it sets the highest enchant tier (normal 1, splash 2, lingering 3), and the tier sets the grade. So lingering is needed for the strongest grade.
- A gem's "other" or "negative" effect from the enchant roll uses the same formula with its own grade and joins that effect's stack.

Total for an effect, in symbols: `total = 0.95 x sum(gem_i x 0.85^(rank_i)) / sum(0.85^0..0.85^11)`, with `gem = potion x base x grade x material x run`.

| Nether quartz | 0.84 | First Nether trip |

Nether star ranks just under diamond in raw strength (0.96), because the owner made diamond the best base, and earns its boss-kill cost with a trait instead. The proposed trait is a beacon-like aura (the beacon is made from a nether star): its effects also reach nearby players at half strength. The trait is an open question; the numbers below don't depend on it.

### How each effect is made partial

| Effect | Implementation | Source (26.3) |
|---|---|---|
| Speed | Attribute modifier on movement_speed, +0.4 x s, add_multiplied_total (exact). | MobEffects.SPEED |
| Strength | Attribute modifier on attack_damage, +6 x s, add_value (exact). | MobEffects.STRENGTH |
| Jump Boost | Attribute modifiers: jump_strength +0.2 x s and safe_fall_distance +2 x s. (Vanilla adds the jump boost after the block jump factor; the attribute is scaled by it, so it is a little weaker on honey.) | MobEffects.JUMP_BOOST, LivingEntity.getJumpBoostPower, Attributes.JUMP_STRENGTH 0.42 |
| Regeneration | Tick handler: heal 0.8 x s / 20 HP per tick while hurt (LivingEntity.heal takes floats). Not a MobEffectInstance, because vanilla levels are whole numbers. | RegenerationMobEffect |
| Resistance (from Turtle Master) | Damage hook (mixin at LivingEntity.getDamageAfterMagicAbsorb, beside vanilla's resistance), x (1 - 0.8 x s), skipping bypasses_resistance damage. | LivingEntity.getDamageAfterMagicAbsorb, Potions.STRONG_TURTLE_MASTER |
| Fire Resistance | On/off made partial: fire-tagged damage (is_fire) x (1 - s) through the damage hook, and burning_time attribute -s (add_multiplied_total) so fire also goes out sooner. | LivingEntity (is_fire + FIRE_RESISTANCE), Entity lava 4.0, Attributes.BURNING_TIME |
| Water Breathing | On/off made partial with the vanilla oxygen_bonus attribute (what Respiration uses): bonus = s / (1 - s), so each air tick is kept with chance s. Pure attribute, exact. | LivingEntity.decreaseAirSupply, Entity.getMaxAirSupply 300 |
| Night Vision | On/off made partial on the client: set the lightmap's nightVisionEffectIntensity to s (mixin at LightmapRenderStateExtractor, where vanilla writes GameRenderer.nightVisionScale). Vanilla already renders fractional values during its end-fade. | GameRenderer.nightVisionScale, LightmapRenderStateExtractor |
| Invisibility | Stealth, not a see-through body: the vanilla mob_visibility item component on each gemmed piece (pieces multiply, so each gets total^(1/n)), plus waypoint_transmit_range -s. Data only. | LivingEntity.getVisibilityPercent, item/component/MobVisibility, MobEffects.INVISIBILITY |
| Slow Falling | On/off made partial: while falling, gravity 0.08 - 0.07 x s (mixin at LivingEntity.getEffectiveGravity, where vanilla checks slow falling) and fall_damage_multiplier -s. | LivingEntity.getEffectiveGravity, Attributes.GRAVITY 0.08 |
| Luck | Attribute modifier on luck, +s (exact). | MobEffects.LUCK |
| Healing | Instant made permanent as an emergency heal: when the wearer drops below half health, heal 8 x s, then a 30 s cooldown. Works the same on mobs. | HealOrHarmMobEffect |
| Harming | Instant made permanent as a charged strike: the first melee hit after a 30 s cooldown deals +12 x s magic damage. Undead targets are healed instead, as in vanilla. | HealOrHarmMobEffect |
| Poison | Offensive: each melee hit poisons the target at 1.67 x s HP/s for 4 s (refreshed, not stacked; never below 1 HP as vanilla). A gem mob effect whose amplifier encodes s in 1% steps keeps vanilla's icon and timer. | PoisonMobEffect |
| Slowness | Offensive: hits slow the target by 60% x s for 4 s. As a negative roll: a permanent movement_speed modifier on the wearer. | MobEffects.SLOWNESS, Potions.STRONG_SLOWNESS |
| Weakness | Offensive: hits weaken the target by 4 x s for 4 s. As a negative roll: a permanent attack_damage modifier on the wearer. | MobEffects.WEAKNESS |
| Wind Charged | Chance-based: the vanilla trigger fires with chance s x vanilla chance. Mob flavour (loot mobs); on players mostly a curiosity. | WindChargedMobEffect |
| Weaving | Chance-based: the vanilla trigger fires with chance s x vanilla chance. Mob flavour (loot mobs); on players mostly a curiosity. | WeavingMobEffect |
| Oozing | Chance-based: the vanilla trigger fires with chance s x vanilla chance. Mob flavour (loot mobs); on players mostly a curiosity. | OozingMobEffect |
| Infested | Chance-based: the vanilla trigger fires with chance s x vanilla chance. Mob flavour (loot mobs); on players mostly a curiosity. | InfestedMobEffect |
| Haste | Attribute modifiers: block_break_speed +0.4 x s and attack_speed +0.2 x s (add_multiplied_total). | Player.getDestroySpeed, MobEffects.HASTE, BeaconBlockEntity |
| Absorption | max_absorption +16 x s, refilled to full 30 s after it was last hit. | AbsorptionMobEffect, Consumables.ENCHANTED_GOLDEN_APPLE |
| Health Boost | Attribute modifier on max_health, +8 x s (exact). | MobEffects.HEALTH_BOOST |
| Dolphin's Grace | On/off made partial: water slow-down 0.8 + 0.16 x s (mixin where travelInWater sets 0.96). | LivingEntity.travelInWater, DOLPHINS_GRACE_WATER_DRAG |
| Mining Fatigue | Attribute modifiers: block_break_speed x 0.027^s (matches levels I-III exactly at s = 1/3, 2/3, 1) and attack_speed -0.3 x s. | Player.getDestroySpeed, ElderGuardian |
| Hunger | Tick handler: causeFoodExhaustion(0.015 x s) per tick. | HungerMobEffect, Consumables.PUFFERFISH |
| Bad Luck | Attribute modifier on luck, -s. | MobEffects.UNLUCK |

Gem effects are attribute modifiers, data components or small tick and damage hooks, not potion effect instances: vanilla levels are whole numbers and their icons and timers would claim a full level. Where a vanilla effect instance is wanted (offensive hits, for the icon and timer on the target), a gem mob effect whose amplifier counts strength in 1% steps does it. A gem and a drunk potion of the same effect don't add up: the stronger applies (open question 10).

## Checks (all passed)

- vanilla facts: 79 facts matched against build/mcsrc/26.3
- every ladder step is at least +4% on the one below
- a gem's own strength reaches 1.0 only from the strongest potion + lingering + tier 3 + diamond, for every effect
- 804,837 armor layouts x gem counts enumerated: only full netherite with 12 gems reaches 0.95; next best 0.922
- from the best build, every single step down (potion, base, tier, material, run, one gem fewer) loses at least 0.025
- weakest single gem (normal potion, amethyst, tier 1, lone leather piece) = 0.034; early kit (iron set, 4 quartz tier-1 gems) = 0.155-0.193
- stacking: 20,000 random stacks never pass 0.95 x their strongest gem; adding a gem never lowers a total; in every armor set 12 best tier-1 gems lose to 4 tier-3 gems
- every in-game mapping rises with strength and stays short of the vanilla level at the cap

## Open questions for the owner

1. Cap at 0.95 (5% short of the strongest potion)? yes / no (0.90 would make the gap easier to feel).
2. Nether star's special part: (a) aura, its effects also reach nearby players at half strength (model's proposal), (b) never rolls a negative, (c) nothing special, it just ranks between ender pearl and diamond.
3. Prismarine base gem: (a) prismarine shard, (b) prismarine crystals.
4. Gold armor: (a) chainmail-level factor 0.83 (model), (b) a magic bonus up to diamond-level 0.93, echoing gold's high enchantability.
5. Turtle helmet counts as its own material (iron-level, always a run of 1)? yes / no.
6. Resistance's 1.0: (a) Resistance IV from strong Turtle Master, 80% less damage (the rule as written; gems up to 76%), (b) Resistance II, the beacon level, 40% (gems up to 38%).
7. Turtle Master gems also carry Turtle Master's Slowness, on the wearer? yes / no.
8. Harmful-potion gems (poison, slowness, weakness, harming) work on what the wearer hits, not on the wearer? yes / no.
9. Healing gems: (a) emergency heal below half health, 30 s cooldown (model), (b) a heal every 30 s regardless.
10. A gem and a drunk potion of the same effect: the stronger applies, they don't add? yes / no.
11. Undead wearers follow vanilla's inversion (a healing gem hurts a zombie, harming heals it)? yes / no.
